# Patch 2.1

# Patch  2.1

## Known Enemy Changes

* Swordy boys who previously had attacks that granted them “Reflection Status” now have “normal” attacks, but now have a passive “Parry” that makes it so they can only receive damage from a source once in a given action, i.e. a burst that chain hits or hits multiple times will only deal 1 hit worth of damage to them. **Note \- Reflection Status as an effect remains unchanged and is still present in the game rarely on some enemies, be cautious and aware when fighting new enemies bow users.** *Adjustment made to more appropriately target the demographic (high damage multi hit/target moves) I was aiming for without severely countering others (good rolls).*

## Enemy Classifications

All Other Enemies remain the same but their strength/classification is more clearly defined. Rubric has been defined according to their rarity for common enemies:

* **Common** \- 10-60 Health, single weak attack (i.e. slimes)  
* **Uncommon** \- 35-125 health, single heavy attack, potentially single weak attack (i.e. Maureen)  
* **Rare** \- 75-175 health, multiple types of attacks, almost always multi-tile larger enemies, very few single tile enemies of this rarity. (i.e. Ruin Guard Robots)  
* **Epic** \- 150-350 health, multiple types of attacks, all decently strong, usually has at least one immunity (i.e. undiscovered, First will be Sumeru Ruin Grader Robot)  
* **Legendary** \- 250-600 health, very painful enemies to fight, essentially single phase bosses. Multiple painful attacks, may or may not come with other smaller enemies on their side, many single tile enemies of this rarity. (i.e. undiscovered, First will be Fontaine Local Legends)

Note that health values will vary a bit from enemy to enemy within these values, in general the closer to the beginning of the game the closer you are to the lowest values, and the closer you are to the end of the game the closer you are to the higher values. These values may be adjusted in the future depending on pacing and difficulty.

## World Boss Criteria

### **General Criteria**

World Bosses have a general pattern of rules made to them to make the game easier for the players. Generally speaking each world boss will have a variety of attacks that have clear indicators and patterns in which they can be avoided or minimized. World bosses will attack after every other action of a player. Additionally world bosses have the following general attributes:

**Phases:** 1-3  
**Total Unique Attacks:** 6-12  
**Health Per Phase:** 50-400  
**Defense Needed To Block Attacks:** 6-16 (should average approximately 10 defense needed)  
**Number of Attacks that penetrate Defense:** 1 or Less  
**Damage Dealt on each Hit:** D4-D12 (should average approximately 1D8 damage per hit)

Upon defeat the world bosses will give a variety of experience, elemental gems, loot, etc. according to ascension level, luck, etc.

## Quest Boss Criteria

### **General Criteria**

Quest Bosses are intended to be tougher than World Bosses. They will have slightly higher HP and/or have tougher requirements in order to clear a particular phase. Additionally the defense rolls needed to block hits on Quest Bosses is generally higher, they will deal more damage, and more of their attacks are able to penetrate defenses. Quest bosses only appear at the end of each region or under powerful character quests (i.e. Zhongli). Quest bosses will attack after every player action. It isn’t uncommon for a player to die during this if not several players. Clearing on your first attempt isn’t guaranteed.

**Phases:** 1-4  
**Total Unique Attacks:** 6-16  
**Health Per Phase:** 100-500  
**Defense Needed To Block Attacks:**10-20 (should average approximately 10 defense needed)  
**Number of Attacks that penetrate Defense:** 2+  
**Damage Dealt on each Hit:** D8+ (should average approximately 10 damage per hit)

The average damage & defense roll requirements should go up by ½ their average ascension level. (i.e. At ascension rank 2 the average defense roll needed to block an attack is 11 instead of 10, at ascension rank 4, this becomes 12, etc.)

Upon defeat the quest bosses will give a variety of experience, elemental gems, loot, etc. according to ascension level, luck, etc.

As with the enemies these values are subject to change for balancing in either direction but are currently set to these values as of this patch.

## 

## Base Stat Changes

* **Base Stats have been reset to 0 for all. Each person now has 45 base points they can choose to allocate** how they wish according to the following rubric:  
  * Health \- 2 Health per point  
  * Attack \- 1 Attack per point  
  * Defense 1 Defense per point  
  * Elemental Mastery \- 1 EM per point  
  * Energy Recharge \- 0.1 ER per point  
  * Critical Damage \- 0.1 CD per point

  Please redistribute your base stats according to your preferences. *Overall compared to before you all will receive a slight stat buff overall in the amount, and a decent buff overall in how they are distributed to your liking.*

* Upon ascending, your stats will continue to reset fully to your base stats. However, **each ascension will allow you to add that ascension level’s worth of points to your Base stats** however you wish (i.e. ascending to rank 3 will give you 3 points to allocate to your Base stats however you wish according to the above rubric). Given that you all are at ascension rank 2 at the time of this patch please allocate an additional 3 base points into your stats however you wish. *Small buff currently, larger buff later on.*  
* **For stat points and dice rolls, rounding remains unchanged for all except D20’s, in order to qualify for a D20 you must get to 20 points. Any less will round down to a D12.** *Small nerf requiring 4 additional points to dice up, meant to encourage having a more balanced stat distribution with only maybe a single stat or two deeply invested to max.*   
* At any point outside of battle a player may “respec” their base stat points if they wish by making an offering to our lord and savior Paimon. Should Paimon accept your offering you can redistribute according to the above base stat rules. *QoL adjustment intended to match the changing elements adjustment made previously.*

## Artifact Changes

* Artifact stats have been slightly adjusted with the following changes:  
  * All artifacts can have Health, Attack, Defense, EM  
  * **Only Sands artifacts can have Energy Recharge**  
  * **Only Circlet artifacts can have Critical Damage**  
  * **Only Goblet artifacts can have a new rare bonus stat: Damage Bonus which adds (or subtracts) a flat amount to any/all damage you deal.**

  Artifact pages have been updated and color coordinated to match their type (i.e. Sands and Energy Recharge are both green so you know which one it needs.) This makes the “optimal” Sands have \+4.0 ER, Circlets \+4.0 CD, and Goblets have \+4 Universal Damage Bonus as these stat boosts are more difficult to come by. *Adjustment that is net neutral overall. CD and ER are now more rare to come by, which is intended to match their stat point distributions, but in exchange players now have a chance at a very rare **universal** flat damage buff.*


## Weapon Changes

* Weapons remain the same but their rarity is more clearly defined. Rubric has been defined according to their rarity:  
  * Common \- 3-4 stat attributes, no effects  
  * Uncommon \- 4-5 stat attributes, weapon effect.  
  * Rare \- 5-6 stat attributes, decent weapon effect.  
  * Epic \- 6-8 Stat attributes, good weapon effect.  
  * Legendary \- 8-10 Stat attributes, great weapon effect.

  Given the above rubric your expectation should generally be: a base weapon of a higher tier should be better than a base weapon of a lower tier. A medium refined weapon of any tier can match the tier above it. A max refined weapon can match, and depending on the effect sometimes exceed, a weapon two tiers above it. (i.e. A refined 2 Rare weapon is comparable and may slightly beat any given Epic weapon depending on effects. A max refined Rare weapon is comparable to a Legendary weapon, the Rare weapon will generally have slightly better stats but a slightly worse effect.


  Stat attributes on weapons work accordingly:

  Health, Attack, Defense, Elemental Mastery: 1 Attribute point \= 1 stat value

  Crit Damage, Energy Recharge: 1 Attribute point \= 0.25 stat value


  Given the rarity of Crit Damage and ER on artifacts they have increased value on weapons. 


  

## Spreadsheet Changes

* Spreadsheets have been updated to have your weapon type automatically update to whatever type of weapon you currently have equipped. Having more than 1 weapon equipped will return a blank weapon type.  
* Spreadsheets have been updated to be more Battlesheet based. While in battle you should (theoretically) only have to be in the Battle tab and generally not have to switch to another tab except in rare cases (i.e. using an item, proccing certain effects mid-fight, etc.)  
* Spreadsheets battle tab has been updated to when someone has an element applied to them a tooltip will be added that shows what reactions could be triggered off of that element and what those effects are.  
* Various Spreadsheet formula fixes have been made to correct broken references resulting in miscalculations of stats.  
* **Enemy count in the battle tab has been reduced from 10 to 8 for laptop screen visibility. More enemies may be active on the map but there will never be more than 8 actively targeting you/moving.**  
* Artifact sheets have been updated to accommodate artifact changes  
* Character sheets have been updated to accommodate artifact changes  
* **Companion sheets have been updated to show all possible companions you could get at the given moment even if they aren’t currently unlocked.**


## Battle Changes

* When in battle, using an item no longer counts as a player’s action, however, movement rules still apply for other attacks. Players may only use a single item per turn. *Buff to items to make them more usable, currently it feels like they are just “oh shit buttons” that are used as a last resort and I’d like to see more interaction between your kits/stats and temporary item buffs in battle.*  
* If you have an active food item that lasts for multiple turns they do not stack, I.e. multiple health over time foods do not stack with each other, using a new one will simply reset the turns left of the active one/replace it. You can however use a food that heals over time followed by an instant health restore food while keeping the heal over time effect.

## 

## Companion Changes

* The free companion you gain at the beginning of the region shall be usable only within that region and will not leave. (i.e. Yaoyao, Thoma)  
* Any companions you permanently unlock (i.e. Childe, Ganyu, HuTao, etc.) can be used anywhere at any time, including story missions of other regions.  
* Units that are unlockable will start at the ascension level of the region they are unlockable from to minimize grinding. I.e. if a companion is unlockable from Liyue, like Zhongli, they will start at ascension 2 as that is the 2nd region.

*There was a dependence upon the radish that I did not like, partly for making her over-tuned for a free unit, partly due to the restrictions around when you could use other options. Free units are now nerfed, all other units are now buffed (and I assure you the permanently unlockable ones are always stronger than the free ones pretty significantly).*

# Patch 2.3

# Patch 2.3

Another small patch, just adding in an experiment to see how well it works before the break so I can tweak it. A Spreadsheet change and very minor balancing changes.

## Spreadsheet Changes

Added a multiplier tab to the character sheets where you could add percentage based damage bonuses in your calculations that will persist in the Battle Tab automatically for you.

Highlighted the fields in the battle tab that are okay to be modified, if it’s not highlighted green don’t touch it.

## Enemy Changes

This is an experimental change to see how it works. Enemies will no longer all use D20’s. Basic enemies will use a D12, higher tier enemies will use a D12+D4 and powerful enemies and bosses will use a D20. In order to hit/block their attack you must roll higher than they do. The damage dealt will be determined by how much higher the roll is rounded down. I.e. if you attack an enemy and roll a 12 and they roll a 5 you will deal 1D6 worth of damage, if the difference is less than 4 you will only deal that difference worth of damage. I.e. you roll a 12 and they roll a 10, you deal 2 damage. 

## Balancing Changes

Kokomi did really good vapes, her healing was more than enough which is intended but her damage was a bit higher than anticipated, I don’t want to discourage using her for the damage though so I made her skill a bit more opportunistic to use. Still get big bops with her skill like you did but now it has a slightly bigger opportunity cost to it. Her burst lasts a while so the charges are increased to compensate, add 2 charges to what you currently have on her.

Yoimiya felt like she was in a weird spot where it wasn’t obvious whether she was a damage dealer or a buffer, as a result she did neither particularly well. So I made both of those a bit better. Still isn’t the best damage dealer nor the best buffer but those are at least more usable on her.

Yae Miko looked a bit clunky and I wasn’t sure if Brian C. would be able to utilize her turrets fully with the cooldown at 6, so I lowered to 4 to make her gameplay feel easier to use around them. Highly recommend Dylan \+ Brian F. review her kit with him as Nathan and I both feel she is actually in a really solid place.

### 

### Kokomi

Skill Cooldown raised from 4 turns to 5\. Burst cost increased from 14 to 16\.

### Yoimiya

Charged attack range increased from 3 to 4\.

Skill duration increased from 2 turns to 3\.

Burst Cost increased from 15 to 17, Instead of marking a single enemy for the buff now marks all enemies hit.

### Yae Miko

Skill Cooldown decreased from 6 to 4\.

### Aqua Simulacra

HP% \+ Damage Bonus increased from 20% to 30%.

## DnD Client \+ Launcher

* A new Launcher \+ Client has been created to facilitate better performance on certain older devices. There are too many features to list here and the patch notes are already long enough but this enables us to build this to function and do exactly what we want it to and is far more customizable and better performing than a web-based spreadsheet ever could.   
* Please download the Launcher at the following link: [https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher/releases](https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher/releases)  
* **Please wait to download and open the launcher until the DnD Session** so that it downloads the latest version. The client is about 500 MB in size  
* You will download the launcher from the latest release above and install it wherever you prefer on your computer (**Note \-** the launcher can be stored anywhere, but for some reason it behaves weird when you download it to say your downloads folder and try to move it somewhere else afterwards. So if you want it stored not in your downloads folder, when you click the file to download the launcher from github make sure the folder location you set there is the final location you want it saved at as it won’t work if you move it afterwards).   
* Running the launcher will automatically check what version of the actual client you have and update it if necessary automatically so you don’t have to worry about downloading a new version every time.  
* The client itself will be stored in your computer’s Documents folder under the “Genshin\_DnD\_Client” folder. Please do not launch this directly as the launcher will manage it for you to make sure you are always up-to-date. That said if you want to see all of the code this program is executing for security purposes (since SOME people think there might be a virus) you can find the original code base open source at this location for each program:  
  * [https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher](https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher)  
  * [https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Client](https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Client)  
* For those worried about security (Brian F.) you will be pleased to know absolutely none of your own info is stored/accessible should someone somehow also find a way to access and download this (Already extremely unlikely) AND hack it to retrieve the stored data (Even more unlikely). You use your email to login but your email is never actually stored, a unique string that I assigned to each of you randomly is added to your entry intermittently, and then encrypted. It then checks for that encrypted match which is what is stored. (i.e. a hypothetical string may be **\#penguins** so when Brian C. enters [dogdos89@gmail.com](mailto:dogdos89@gmail.com) it loads it as [d**\#**o**p**g**e**d**n**o**g**s**u**8**i**9**ns**@gmail.com](http://dogdos89@gmail.com#penguins) and then encrypts that entry making it so the final result of an entry similar to this might be: **2b63a68f30bac3c6308071ee0c209399bb6f8111ea3709e3c1bad6902893fa9a** which is what is stored as your unique identifiers. All other info that is stored is based on the actual campaign itself and not personal to you in any way shape or form. You have a significantly higher risk of your email getting exposed by having a facebook/amazon account than this and your email is the only personal piece of information used as a login identifier. If you are still concerned about this, message me and we can set up a custom value you’d put in to login that isn’t your email.  
* Bugs or issues encountered at any point can be reported using the feedback button ![][image2]  
* This button will be available/accessible on every major screen in the client. Hitting this button will trigger a feedback popup for you to fill out to describe where the issue is:

![][image3]  
Hitting the submit feedback button sends the feedback directly to me to review and fix. If we are in the middle of a session when you encounter something please submit the feedback as I can’t correct the client mid-session. I will however have access to everything on the backend to be able to manually override any fixes as needed so also let me know when you submit feedback if it’s something like your stats are wrong or you’re missing an item or damage doesn’t go through, or something of that nature.

I did take into account your preferences to have the order matter. Note as with all reactions any referenced damage is additional REACTION damage, separate from any damage the attack itself may do and any multipliers said attack may have (i.e. crits) unless it specifies otherwise.

They additionally add \+4 to their next defense roll. | You chuck a rock at each of your allies' faces, blinding them and making their attacks hit a random target regardless of their selection for 2 turns. |

## 

## Status Changes

* The following Statuses that existed are not changed per se but we are adding clarification and definitions for everything, as things happened that shouldn’t have. Other effects are entirely new:  
  * **Stunned \-** Your turn is essentially skipped, you cannot act or do anything. If you have an ability that lets you do something “at any time” you cannot do them while stunned. (i.e. duration of 1 turn means until the end of your next turn).  
  * **Rooted \-** You may still act fully but cannot move in any way. If the ability you are trying to use has movement (i.e. blinks,dashes) built into it you cannot use it while rooted.  
  * **Blinded \-** You may target whoever you want but a dice will be rolled and the target will change to whoever the dice indicates. If it is an AoE ability it will apply an AoE centered optimally around that new target. **Friendly fire is turned on** for any blinded attacks.  
  * **Reflect \-** The attack that would hit the target is reflected back at the attacker.  
  * **Slowed \-** Each tile of movement counts as 2 rather than 1\.  
  * **Quickened \-** Each tile of movement counts as ½ rather than 1\.  
  * **Advantage \-** You roll 2 dice rolls and take the better of the two.  
  * **Disadvantage \-** You roll 2 dice rolls and take the worse of the two.  
  * **Camouflaged \-** You cannot be seen by enemies until the camouflage ends or you attack someone (using heals or such on your allies counts).  
  * **Disarm \-** Weapon is knocked away from the unit, cannot attack until weapon is recovered. May swap to a weapon in inventory of the same type (counts as action). If a weapon is not picked up by battle end it is lost. Typically a condition unique to Brian C.  
  * **Taunt \-** Forces enemies to attack the taunting unit.  
  * **Fear \-** Forces enemies to move away/target the furthest ally away from the fearing unit.  
  * **Burst Busted \-** Cannot generate burst charges while active.  
  * **CD Choused \-** Cooldowns do not decrease while active.  
  * **Unlucky \-** Overrides Luck and makes bad things happen.  
  * **Lucky \-** Overrides Luck and makes good things happen.  
  * **En Garde \-** The attack against this unit deals no damage and the attacker is stunned for 1 turn.  
    

More Status Effects may be added in the future. 

Multiple Status Conditions may be on you at once for varying durations per popular vote. Sometimes they may cancel out (i.e. if you are affected by both a slow and quicken you will just move at normal speed until one of them ends).

## Stat Calculations

* There were many fields you would have manual control over to determine your stats. Now the vast majority should be automatically calculated correctly by the client. This includes most artifact set effects, food buff effects, and some weapon effects. ## Character Introduction

### Bennett

Please meet Bennett, an adventurer like you who travels around Teyvat.

“*One of the few young adventurers of the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild, he is always plagued with inexplicable bad luck.*  
*He is the only active member of his own adventure group, known as "Benny's Adventure Team," after all the other members decided to "take leave" following a series of unfortunate incidents. As a result, the team is currently on the verge of being dissolved.*  
*Being unable to break the poor boy's heart, Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild has kept "Benny's Adventure Team" on the books, whilst also hiding from him the fact that all the other members have long since officially left the team.*”

![][image6]

## For reference of how bad Benny’s luck is, this is his in game idle animation:

![][image7]  
Yup random rocks will literally fall from the sky to hit him in the head.

#### Bennett’s Kit:

**Skill \-** Empowers his sword with fire and swipes upwards in any adjacent direction, hitting all enemies up to 3 tiles out. Due to Bennett's luck he is unable to finish smoothly though and this swipe blows up in his face knocking him and any adjacent allies back 2 tiles in the opposite direction afterwards.

**Burst \-** Summons a flaming field 3 tiles out around Bennett in every direction for 3 turns. At the start of Bennett's turn heal all party members inside for 2 health. Anyone (**including enemies**) attacking from within the field, or are attacked while standing in the field shall have the damage converted to fire damage (Uses their normal dice for Rolls still), additionally any **base\_damage** (Any attack that actually hits on its own accord) dealt shall be increased by **1\* Avg Attack** roll (limit only on the first hit per target).

**Passive \-** If Bennett was used in your last battle, until the next battle all party members will have their daily luck reduced by 25%.

As you can see Bennett is arguably the best buffer in the game, in theory, if you attack near him he will make all of your attacks become nukes; however, due to his luck enemies also have the ability to use this buff. (i.e. if your avg attack roll is 12, you will all have 12 added to your damage dealt **pre-multiplier**, if you hit on any attacks within his range. However, enemies will also have 12 added to their attacks if they hit within range).   
It’s worth noting that like all damage buffs, unless specified, damage buffs only apply if you actually hit and would deal damage, if your attack roll misses the buff will do nothing. 

Also Note that Benny is an icon, while chances are likely his numbers will adjust as you start figuring out ways to abuse him, his role as arguably the best buffer in the game for most people is an iconic meme and will persist regardless of where his numbers end up. While not specific to right now, this copypasta is pretty universal on him:

“*I can't take it anymore. I'm sick of bennett. I try to play mavuika. She needs bennett. I try to play lyney. He needs bennett. I try to play navia. She needs bennett. I give up and try to play xiangling. Her best teams all have bennett. I want to play raiden, childe, diluc, arlecchino, gaming, kinich, chasca, wriothesley. They all want bennett.*

*I log in every day and choose my team. "Benny's adventure team, ASSEMBLE." Every quest, every event, every abyss his circle is sitting there on the ground taunting me 👍 while I play circle impact. I need to get my burst back "Let's LIGHT IT UP" I hear. I can't even clear abyss, all my teams need bennett. "You can clear easily,” he tells me, “just pull an HP scaler like neuvillette.*

*I try to pull for neuvillette, I lose the 50/50. Looks like bennett's adventure team is unlucky again. I try to clear abyss anyway, the hydro tulpa vaporizes on bennett's pyro infusion and one-shots me. What a cruel world.”*

![][image8]

## Companion Changes

## Companions have been adjusted quite drastically in many ways. First off, they behave much more similarly to you now in the sense that **they can now hold and use items in battle.** They have stats equal to the average of the entire party in every way.**They cannot use/equip any artifacts** as I feel like you already have a hard enough time finding good pieces for yourself barring a certain shocky boi. Open to feedback regarding this though. They **will** be able to equip weapons soon, but as of right now this is not yet implemented.  In addition to these adjustments, **companions also now have set health** in battle, they can go down just like you and require soups to revive just like you all do. Unlike you all, if a battle is ended with a companion down, **THEY ARE DEAD.** Watch out for stray, allegedly allied, thunderclouds. There are some more alterations regarding companions but I will leave those for you to discover as you adventure around Teyvat with the bestest guide Paimon\! 

## Ability/Kit Changes

## Systematically the game has been modified to rather than having a set basic, charged, skill, and burst all abilities are modular and limitless. While nothing about your specific kits have changed yet, just know this opens up the possibilities, kits like your entire kit being just 10 different types of basic attacks or no burst kits, or only burst kits \+ charged attacks, etc.   In addition to the new modular nature of abilities there are also now new types of abilities \- **Passive abilities**. Like you’d expect they aren’t anything you have to act on or do in battle, they will just be present for you to keep in mind. For example some time in the future older and more disliked kits may gain new passives to help buff them up to par with where they should be. Or some kits that require stacking mechanics will have a passive explaining those stacks.

In addition to these passives now being present you will have a way to track your stacks automatically for those abilities as part of the new client. It will prompt you for them like it would your burst charges on your turn and keep track of where you’re at from there.

On top of the abilities themselves being modular, as are their properties. This means there may be new types of extra powerful skills or charged attacks that you can use but consume a small amount of burst charges on use making them feel more unique, or basic attacks and bursts that have a turn cooldown on use.

## Gambling Character Acquisition

There’s a lot of characters and you have to complete their quest to unlock them as a companion so we are implementing a way for you to acquire characters faster without their quest and to throw in some spice for it. 

**For 500 Mora (gold), you can do a dice roll to earn a Character Gamble**. If you are successful with your dice roll and earn a Gamble you may choose to double or nothing it, with another dice roll for free or keep the gamble as is. **With 10 Character Gambles you will unlock a random locked character from those available to you for free.** Character Gambles will also be earned in other methods and are NOT sellable. 

Daily luck does **slightly** impact your chances with the dice roll; however, **you MUST take ordered turns with the rolls**, the same person cannot do all of the gamble rolls in a row. Note there are a very small handful of characters that canonically require their quest to even become characters you can play or something similar, in these few rare cases if you land on them I’ll just have you reroll as the quest IS required in those cases (i.e. the archons/gods for one example.)

## Party Changes

Some things have been modified to be party-wide rather than individual specific. Character Gambles mentioned above are party-wide. Additionally Mora (Gold) has been modified to be party-wide (you were functionally using it party-wide anyways just having one person hold it then grabbing from them when needed).

## Cautionary Note

I have added a lot of things that now calculate automatically, that said not everything does and I’m bad at math. There are still some effects that do not update on their own or are updating wrong and you will have to keep in mind when you are doing your turn. The way the system is processed you can manually correct it all the way up to the point you click the **“end turn”** button. If you forget a buff or effect after that point it’s considered lost damage. Again if you are ever unsure if something is or is not calculated when doing something you just need to click on that stat during the player hub or during your turn which will tell you where it pulls everything from.

## Balance Changes

### Multi-hit/AoE Damage Adjustment

The following changes have been made regarding moves that hit the same target many times:

Successive hits on any target for a single attack will have diminishing returns per hit unless specified otherwise. I.e.

* 1st Hit \- 100% / Full Damage  
* 2nd Hit 33% / 1/3rd Damage  
* 3rd Hit 11% 1/9th Damage  
* 4th Hit 3.6% 1/27th Damage  
* etc.

Reviewing the logs, **this change as described above does not impact or alter the outcome of any battle situation that has happened up to this point** but makes things more manageable to balance and account for. 

For example, the largest hit last session came from Dylan who did a total of 1680 damage in a single turn. This damage was spread out across 5 enemies doing 96 damage to a small slime and 396 damage to each of the other 4 larger enemies. 

Using the above logic this attack would instead have dealt 664 damage, 96 to the small slime for the first hit still getting full power, and 142 damage to each of the other 4 enemies (96 1st hit, 32 2nd hit, 11 3rd hit, 3 4th hit). **142 damage is enough to 1 shot the vast majority of enemies** you will currently encounter so all still would have died from this attack regardless (as they should have because it was a genuinely good roll). 

This enables significantly easier balancing and does work for multi-hit moves from opponents as well. Several enemies, bosses included, have attacks that hit you multiple times and the above rules will apply to those attacks universally too. You are still not capped on damage in any way and the number can go as big as you’re able to make it, it just makes it more difficult to achieve a cosmetically silly number beyond just killing them. If you want to hit that 1680 you can still, you just have to really earn it now.

There will be several abilities adjusted below to accommodate this as well with some exceptions but the general rule of thumb is the easier/looser the rules are for the ability the more likely this effect applies to that attack, the more difficult/situational an attack/aoe is to hit properly the less likely this rule is to apply. 

For example, in Dylan’s wind kit his burst just fires out a large AoE hitting any enemy within 5 tiles, this has no rules/stipulations and a large area so it will get the above effect. 

On the inverse of that, Dylan’s electric catalyst kit requires AoE hits to travel in a line between him and his cloud’s position and only chains out straight from the previous target that was hit in said line. Given the many conditions/stipulations around this ability’s setup and how the AoE/chain hits can apply it will have a specified exception to the above rule and deal full damage on all hits.

Speaking to the aspect of the benefit of it, you all fought the Cryo Regisvine that shot out up to a D12 number of icicles at a player in one of their attacks (i.e. a rolled 10 meant 10 icicle hits inbound). This rule applies to situations like this as well (unless specified otherwise) so the first icicle may have dealt 9 damage, the second 3, and the remaining 8 icicles 1 damage each rather than each doing a full 9 damage.

## Marketing Bug Compensation

Several bugs were discovered in the market. The first of which was that no logs for any marketing functions were created meaning I have no way to see what was bought or sold at any given point. This alone is not the end of the world but the more egregious issue is that item selling was never actually set up properly from a functional perspective. This essentially enabled the situation where you all, unknowingly, were able to create literally tens of thousands of gold/mora for free while still keeping all items you attempted to sell. 

This issue combined with the fact that I have no history of these transactions means things got very broken and busted. The only resolution I have for this as a DM is to do a rollback on the respective items and gold tables to what they were before the last session. 

I do have transactions for materials gathered and items crafted so I will restore those interactions after rolling back the data however any items bought or sold via the market will be gone as I have no way to see all of the transactions made for the last session.

This is entirely an error caused by my side in the software and was not intentional or planned at all. As such, you shall receive 5 character gambles for free as compensation (valued at approximately 5000 gold) for this error.

Any items you sold will still be in your inventory, and any items you bought will be gone.

## Market Changes

Logging functionality has been added for every interaction within the market. Anytime you buy or sell something, full details of this exchange are logged to account for it so should any bugs or issues popup within the client we can have full detailed information of said changes.

The following values have been changed regarding the market values:

**Base Sell Rate (before luck and variance appliers):**

40% \> 20%

**Sell Rate Minimum Value (after luck and variance appliers):**

15% \> 10%

**Sell Rate Maximum Value (after luck and variance appliers):**

50% \> 30 %

Essentially what the above numbers mean is by default you will have a base sell rate of 20% item value, should you have bad luck and the item be a common item in high stock for that region it can go as low as 10% item value for your sell price and if the item is rare and/or in low stock for the region and you have good luck it can go as high as 30% item value. It is by design that you have a very low sell value to stop money glitches around crafting and to make you consider selling vs crafting or exchanging in more special market encounters. This should feel like you’re selling to a pawn shop and getting ripped off as the intended result.

### Artifact Pricing

Artifacts were priced way too cheaply before, more specifically really good artifacts. Pricing has been adjusted so all artifacts in general will be slightly more expensive than before (i.e. bad artifacts used to be around 20-30 gold, and are now around 40-50 gold. Decent artifacts went from 100-200 gold, to around 400-500 gold. Goated artifacts went from around 1000-2000 gold to 5000-15000.) Note these are final buy values of the artifact, the base value is now similar to the weapon values listed below with the truly goated artifacts being slightly higher in base value than legendary weapons. 

You should still be able to find a “decent” enough set for a reasonable price but if you encounter an artifact that is truly an insanely good piece, it will now cost an insanely high amount. 

### Weapon Pricing

Weapons were priced fairly accurately for the most part. That said I wanted a bit more distinguishing between “common” weapons and more rare ones:

**Legendary Weapons Base Value:**

4000 \> 6000

**Epic Weapons Base Value:**

2000 \> 3000

**Rare Weapons Base Value:**

1000 \> 850

These are their base values pre-multipliers. There are multipliers that will increase/decrease them based on scarcity, if the item is commonly found in that specific region, your luck, etc.

### 

### Consumables Pricing

None of the consumables had prices/values previously set allowing you to get fully crafted foods for pennies incorrectly. Item values have been updated for all consumables to now appropriately account for the cost of the items required to make them.

### Stock Refreshes

The stock and prices within the market for things you can buy were previously set to refresh every time you opened the respective screen/tab. This enabled the behavior to spam refresh until you got the item or price that you desired. 

This has been updated so it now sets it each time you return to town. Stock will still be different for each player but will no longer update/change on each refresh of the tab/view. Every time you are in town the items you can buy are refreshed. You can open and close the market as much as you want and the buy-items will remain the same until you all go out and do something. Selling items will still ever so slightly adjust your sell price in slight variations as overhauling this will require a larger refactor that I don’t want to do right now.

### Selling Items

Selling an item now correctly removes that item amount from your character. This was previously broken due to the super fun typo of me referring to tables with spaces as say “Character Artifacts” rather than what it should have been with an underscore of “Character\_Artifacts”

Sold artifacts were also not updating in the local clients even though the change itself was being recorded on the server side. This has been updated to correctly sync artifact changes on your local client. So for example when you sell an artifact it will now correctly refresh your UI automatically to update and show said artifact is now gone.

## Status Effects

Status Effects exist exactly how they did as described in the previous patch notes, now however, if you have an ability that specifies that it applies one of those effects, those effects will automatically apply from said ability with the specified duration onto your targets.

Status Effects caused from bad rolls or reactions is not yet implemented and must be done manually by me.

## Roadmap

1. Give Weapons/Artifacts from one person to another  
2. Implement functional shields in combat.  
3. Minigames  
4. Add Enemy Fog of War (i.e. I add an enemy that is there in the battle but doesn’t show up in UI until you make it to them on the actual board itself.)

# Patch 3.2

## System Issues

The Server Side Client has been fixed (**I think**). I did quite a bit of significant updating on the server side as the last time I touched this was in July when I first started this project and a lot has changed on it since then. Now should the server ever crash it properly logs and records the crash and the trigger. Additionally it keeps a log of everything it receives from its end as well as any non-crashing errors. Old systems that are no longer used in the project (i.e. On-Render (replaced by Cloudflare), Airtable (Replaced by me hosting the DB locally) have been fully removed from the server side.

Please download the latest version of the **Launcher** located here:  
[https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher/releases/tag/0.2.1](https://github.com/SturdyGhost/GI-Anime-Game-DnD-Launcher/releases/tag/0.2.1)  
Please note that there are now 2 files present, please download and keep both of them in whatever file location you prefer. You will most commonly run and use “**Genshin.DnD.Launcher.exe**” but if you ever run into issues you will then swap over to “**Genshin.DnD.Launcher.console.exe**” which will give you a lot more pertinent information as to why you ran into the issues you did.

As before the **Client** version can be found in your documents folder and run directly under extreme problems. 

## Client New Features

Below is a list of new features added to the client. Some of the more complex features will also have their own sections in the notes to elaborate on them more.

* Selecting the “**Settings**” button on the Town menu now opens a settings menu to adjust or turn off the volume of any playing music within the client (That said I would fully recommend listening to their music, they get huge orchestra’s to do their music and are widely regarded as producing some of the better video game music sound tracks, I would especially recommend their “Nod Krai” album, it has big instrumental DnD vibes).  
* Players now have the ability to give “Weapons” to one another from the Weapons menu.  
* Players now have the ability to give “Artifacts” to one another from the respective Artifact Pieces Menu.  
* A new “Minigames” menu has been enabled, more on it below.  
* Shields are now fully functional in combat (in theory), more on it below.  
* Fog of war is now functional in combat (in theory), meaning when you go into battle, what you see on the battle screen may or may not be the full list of enemies in that encounter.




## Market Adjustments

The market changes from last session largely landed where I wanted them to where you all had to contemplate the tradeoffs of selling your items vs keeping them to have backups and what value you were truly getting from selling since it wasn’t a good deal (i.e. pawn shop offer). 

That said, one of the features I did for the “Buy” tab was make it so you couldn’t spam refresh to update offers, this feature has now also been corrected/added to the “Sell” tab. The offer you get is your active offer for that item until you go out into a combat session, upon returning and time having passed a new offer for that item will be present.

## Unit Distance Calculation

It already worked this way in the last 2 sessions we did but just to affirm, if you have an ability that says it can target any unit/tile within say 6 tiles, that distance is calculated the same way your movement is calculated, i.e. the 4 adjacent directions, not diagonal directions.

## 

## Status Effects

The following [Status Effects]() have been added to the game:

* **Collateral Damage \-** When you deal damage to a target, ¼ of the final damage dealt to them is also dealt to the ally closest to you.  
* **Dazed \-** You must act, but only using Basic Attacks. Skills and Bursts cannot be used.  
* **Slippery \-** The next time you move, you slide your full movement straight in that direction unable to stop any sooner.  
* **Pinned \-** You may not rotate or change facing direction.  
* **Hot Feet \-** Before attacking you must use your full movement of the desired ability. If movement is needed you cannot end on the tile you started on.  
* **Overheated \-** Using an ability with a turn cooldown increases its cooldown by 1 additional turn.  
* **Locked In \-** You must repeat the same actions you took last turn in the same order if possible.  
* **Loner \-** Ending your turn on a tile with any entity on surrounding tiles causes your next attack to deal no damage.  
* **Shield-Break  \-** Any incoming damage is doubled. While this status is active, I cannot gain a new shield and cannot eat any food items.

Note you won’t see many status effects yet as they have to be manually set. The only functional status effect you will see is “Shield-Break”. All other status effects have yet to be properly assigned/built out in the ability/attack that triggers them yet. That will be the next project.

## Shields

Shields have some similar mechanics as before but are receiving some overhaul with some balance adjustment. First off they are now implemented into the client UI in battle. If a unit has a shield they will have a metallic looking border around their character card. There is also UI added to show how much shield health it has left as well as how many turns it has left.

In battle, **shields are now directional and move/rotate with your character**. By default your shield will cover one of the 4 directions unless multiple/all directions are specified in the ability. This means they no longer universally cover all 4 directions like before. However this also means that you have control over when your shield is or is not used to absorb damage from attacks, maybe you want to save it for a specific big attack on a boss (required in some cases to survive the attack, big damage to non-shielded units), or maybe you aren’t concerned with absorbing attacks from certain creatures and don’t want to risk getting the shield-break debuff. Shield duration has been increased to accommodate more nuance/play with their directions.

All elements create the same shield. They will last for a set number of turns or until they run out of health. When a shield **runs out of health** (not expires from turns) the entity that had the shield will receive the “Shield-Break” status for 2 turns as an enemy inflicted enough damage to break said shield.

In terms of UI here are what the enemy cards will look like with vs without a shield:![][image9]

Note the text in the shield icons IS small, but it’s supplemental, the “+” icon shield is health, and the circular arrow is duration/turns left so those should be what are used to recognize it, the small text labels are just a backup precaution. The text is also not quite as unreadable as the screenshots make them out to be. Submit feedback if you find the labels to be unreadable for you in experience.

Note Status Effects look wonky right now and will be getting reworked next time.

Below is what the companion/party cards will look like with the shield:![][image10]  
Like with the enemies it will have a gray border around the whole card, and icons will popup indicating a shield is present with corresponding durations and health values.

When a shield’s health or duration reaches 0 it is removed from that character. If it is removed from the health becoming 0, that character shall receive the “Shield-Break” status effect for 2 turns.  
When it is your turn and you are setting all of your info/actions for your turn, on each target there are a few new fields for you. The first is a new “damage type” selector named “Shielded”. When you generate a shield for an ally you’ll put in the total health of the shield in the “Amount” field and then make sure the damage type is set to “Shielded”. Upon ending your turn it will generate a shield for that target in that amount. **Unless specified otherwise the default length is 4 turns.**

Additionally when you are damaging someone, if they have a shield there is a new toggle named “Hit Shield” that is only enabled/clickable if that target has an active shield. If they do when you attack them you may or may not hit the shield depending on your location as described above. If your attack does hit their shield check that box, if not leave it unchecked. Only attacks that hit the shield will interact with it.

![][image11] ![][image12]

## 

## Fog of War

There will now be a “fog of war” mechanic on maps, so you won’t necessarily be seeing the total number of enemies at once, you may discover some new ones on the map when you go into a room for example. Enemies hidden by fog of war cannot be seen on the physical board and will not show up in the client battle menu until you have triggered seeing them on the physical board. 

After triggering them on the physical board the battle ui will automatically update to account for the new enemies showing up in the list.

## Minigames

You now have the “Minigames” button unlocked while you are in town. **Minigames are entirely optional** little side games you can play as a means of killing time while you’re waiting, for example if Brian C. is in the middle of a research session Dylan has downtime to go and play a minigame if he wants to.

Playing a minigame gives you a **small** amount of rewards if you do well enough at it. These rewards come in the form of regional materials, similar to gathering but much less in amount. It will also show a small high score system so you can see which of you have done the best at any given minigame if you’re interested in competing for that.

As of now there is only one minigame present in the list for you to choose from, Fish Blasting With Klee. You move your mouse around and press space bar to launch a bomb, your goal is to blast as many fish as possible.

If you have any ideas or wants for a specific type of minigame, again quick small one off little games, then please submit it as feedback and I will add it to my list to work on.

## Logging/Troubleshooting

We’ve had some issues with the client in the past during sessions not doing what they’re supposed to. I obviously can manually adjust everything and every action that is done is logged to the Database should things majorly break, that said in the heat of the moment you won’t necessarily know what happened or went wrong. 

To support this like I mentioned above there is now an optional console file included for you to optionally download if you want. This console version will print out any logs that happen to be documented. Historically there wasn’t much in the logs but a big part of my updates this month has been going through and adding extreme amounts of logging on everything so that should something fail it will let us know what failed and where it failed at. 

As an example below is the logs that happen from when any of you enter your email and hit login to when the client fully loads onto your town hub screen:

## Roadmap

The following are things on my list currently, this is open to feedback and requests made by y’all:

* Going through the data and adding in status effects on moves/abilities. The client supports applying them automatically but no moves currently have them.  
* Adding new minigames that fit what you all want to see.  
* Switching to Websockets (currently uses asynchronous polling).  
* Overhauling/redoing the combat scene (it’s a mess with the polling right now and wasn’t built cleanly, now that we have a full understanding of all that happens in combat it really needs to get rebuilt at some point.)
